text: Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 46 already covered shares, providers, recipients, and the headline feature: a recipient doesn't need Databricks to read a shared table. This lesson is what's actually happening underneath that CREATE SHARE statement.

A recipient's client makes REST calls to a Delta Sharing Server — list shares, list tables, get metadata, get pre-signed URLs to the underlying Parquet files — then reads those files directly. That's why a non-Databricks client can participate at all.

If the recipient also runs Unity Catalog, the shared table can appear directly in their own catalog with no credential file at all. Open sharing is what makes a plain Python or Power BI recipient possible, at the cost of managing a credential file themselves.

A plain shared table gives only the current snapshot. Sharing with history lets the recipient read version history and Change Data Feed through the same protocol, pulling incremental changes instead of re-reading the whole table every time.
Snapshot versus history is the real distinction between Delta Sharing and just exporting a file. Next up: secrets management, and keeping credentials out of code entirely.
